overview.title: 📖 Overview: Tracing the Decrees to Their Origins
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 15a–15b
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens by distinguishing Solomon's original decree, which covered only consecrated items, from the later decree extending impurity concerns to teruma as well. It then catalogs the only three matters Hillel and Shammai personally disputed — the measure for ḥalla, how much drawn water disqualifies a ritual bath, and a difficult question about a niddah's uncertain flow — before tracing several other decrees, including the impurity of foreign land and of glass vessels, back through layered historical stages to their true origins.

slides.title: 🍇 Two Near-Disputes, Explained Away
slides.subtitle: Why the tally still stays at exactly three

lines.speaker: Question
lines.text: Only three disputes? What about laying hands (semikha) on festival offerings — Hillel permits it, Shammai forbids it?

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: That dispute is far older, going back to Sages who preceded them; Rav Huna meant only disputes original to Hillel and Shammai themselves.

lines.speaker: Question
lines.text: What about one who harvests grapes for the press — Shammai says the seeping juice renders them susceptible to impurity, Hillel says it does not?

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: Except for that one case — there, Hillel ultimately fell silent and did not respond to Shammai, effectively conceding the point.

slides.title: 📅 180, 80, 40 Years Before the Destruction
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, reports his father's chronology

steps.content: 1️⃣ When Rabbi Yishmael ben Rabbi Yosei fell ill, the Sages asked him to share teachings he once heard from his father
2️⃣ 180 years before the Temple's destruction: the evil kingdom of Rome invaded the land
3️⃣ 80 years before the destruction: the Sages decreed impurity on the land of the nations and on glass vessels
4️⃣ 40 years before the destruction: the Sanhedrin left the Chamber of Hewn Stone for the stores on the Temple Mount — meaning it no longer judged capital cases

slides.title: 🌍 The Staged Decree on the Land of the Nations
slides.subtitle: Reconciling early Sages with a late timeline

nodes.content: ❓ Yosei ben Yo'ezer and Yosei ben Yoḥanan lived generations before the '80 years before the destruction' — so how could they be the ones who decreed on foreign land?
1️⃣ Yosei ben Yo'ezer and Yosei ben Yoḥanan: teruma touching a clod of foreign earth is held 'in abeyance'; nothing said yet about its airspace
2️⃣ The Sages of the last 80 years: extend 'in abeyance' to the airspace of foreign lands too
3️⃣ The Sages of Usha (after the destruction): upgrade contact with the clod itself to 'burn' — its airspace remains merely in abeyance

callout.label: Six related uncertainties:
callout.text: A related mishna lists six cases of uncertain impurity — beit haperas, foreign earth, an am ha'aretz's clothing, a found vessel, spittle, and urine — where definite contact still requires teruma to be burned, even though the impurity itself is only in doubt.

slides.title: 🔮 Glass Vessels — Earthenware or Metal?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yoḥanan's ruling, tested against a puzzling mishna

boxes.title: Like earthenware
items: Rabbi Yoḥanan (citing Reish Lakish): since glass begins from sand, the Sages equated it with earthenware
Problem: earthenware vessels are never purified by immersion — yet a mishna treats glass vessels as immersible

boxes.title: The special exception
items: A perforated glass vessel patched by dripping in molten lead
Rabbi Meir: 'everything follows the reinforcing material' — since lead (a metal) can be purified by immersion, so can this vessel

boxes.title: The Rabbis disagree
items: The Rabbis deem such a lead-patched glass vessel ritually pure regardless, rejecting Rabbi Meir's 'follows the facilitator' principle here

summary.principle: Behind the eighteen decrees lies a careful historical record: only three disputes were ever truly Hillel's and Shammai's own, and decrees like those on foreign land and glass vessels grew in stages across generations, from early Sages through the last decades before the Temple's fall and beyond.

quiz.q: What compromise did the Rabbis reach on the minimum dough obligated in ḥalla, between Shammai's one kav and Hillel's two kav?
o: Exactly one kav
Exactly two kav
One and a half kav
Three kav
quiz.e: The Rabbis ruled neither like Shammai nor like Hillel, but at one and a half kav (later recalibrated as measures changed).

quiz.q: How much drawn water was ultimately established to disqualify a ritual bath, according to the testimony of two weavers in the name of Shemaya and Avtalyon?
o: Nine kav
A full hin (twelve log)
Three log
One se'ah
quiz.e: The Sages upheld the weavers' testimony that three log of drawn water disqualifies a ritual bath, overriding both Hillel's and Shammai's larger measures.

quiz.q: Why doesn't the Gemara count the dispute over laying hands (semikha) on festival offerings as one of Hillel and Shammai's own three disputes?
o: Because they never actually discussed the topic
Because it is an ancient dispute that predates them
Because Rabbi Meir later resolved it
Because it only concerns Temple-era practice
quiz.e: The Gemara explains that this dispute over semikha goes back to Sages who came before Hillel and Shammai, so it is not counted among their own original three disagreements.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yishmael ben Yosei's report of his father's teaching, what marked forty years before the Temple's destruction?
o: Rome first invaded the land
The decree of impurity on the land of the nations and glass vessels
The Sanhedrin left the Chamber of Hewn Stone, meaning it no longer judged capital cases
The eighteen decrees were formally ratified
quiz.e: Forty years before the destruction, the Sanhedrin relocated from the Chamber of Hewn Stone to the stores on the Temple Mount, understood to mean it ceased judging capital cases.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara resolve the tension between equating glass with earthenware (which cannot be purified by immersion) and a mishna suggesting glass vessels can be purified by immersion?
o: It rejects the mishna as unreliable
It explains the mishna refers to a perforated glass vessel patched with lead, which Rabbi Meir treats as following the metal that reinforces it
It says all glass vessels are always impure regardless of immersion
It claims glass vessels were never actually equated with earthenware
quiz.e: The Gemara explains the mishna's case involves glass sealed with dripped lead; Rabbi Meir holds that such a vessel follows the status of its reinforcing material — lead, a metal that can be purified by immersion.
